official.deadline_note: The 2026/2027 Postgraduate Foreign Scholarship window ran from 13 April 2026 and closed on 30 April 2026, so it has now closed. GETFund issues the foreign scholarship call annually, so the next round is expected in the first half of 2027. Note that the how-to-apply page still displays the earlier 2024/25 call dates (20 January to 20 February 2025) as its dated example, so the news page is the reliable source for the current window.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year call (applications 13 April 2026 to 30 April 2026)
official.status_note: GETFund announced that applications for its Postgraduate Foreign Scholarship Programme for the 2026/2027 academic year opened on 13 April 2026 and closed on 30 April 2026. A separate, later round for the 2026/27 Undergraduate and Postgraduate LOCAL scholarships was announced on 2 October 2026, which is a different scheme and not the foreign scholarship.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The programme overview states: "The Program provides financial, social, and academic support to Scholars. Financial support includes tuition fees, accommodation, and scholastic materials." The how-to-apply page states that foreign scholarship coverage "Typically covers tuition, accommodation, and sometimes stipend for living expenses. Specific details regarding partial or full scholarship will be provided upon award."
benefits: Financial support including tuition fees, accommodation and scholastic materials
Social and academic support to scholars alongside the financial award

Priority consideration for applicants pursuing STEM, TVET, special needs programmes, National Initiative Priority programmes, programmes at tuition-free universities, lecturers of public tertiary institutions (via GTEC) and persons with special needs
Faculty development support through the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission for university lecturers pursuing further education abroad
Programme scale: 1,586 undergraduate scholars, 3,448 masters scholars and 487 PhD scholars supported alongside 697 executive education programmes
eligibility: Must have obtained admission to undertake a Masters programme (or Undergraduate-Medicine only, Eastern Europe and Asia)
Must hold a first degree of at least second class (for Master's applicants)
Must be available to start academic studies by the start of the academic year for which sponsorship is sought
Applicant must not be pursuing a PhD or Master's degree at the time of application
Should not be a previous beneficiary of a GETFund Foreign Scholarship applying for the same scholarship category
requirements: Apply through the GETFund scholarship portal: create a profile, verify the account, complete the application form and upload the required documents
Submit an admission letter from an accredited university - unconditional and financial condition letters only - together with the fee schedule
Submit a project or research proposal not exceeding five pages (Masters and PhD applicants)
Complete and submit the application before the deadline and respond to vetting and shortlisting communications
Accept that the scholarship must be used for the academic year awarded - deferment is not allowed
documents: Admission letter from an accredited university (unconditional and financial condition letters only) plus the fee schedule
Previous academic certificates and previous transcript (where applicable)
Project or research proposal not exceeding five pages (Masters and PhD applicants)
Curriculum vitae, academic referees and a letter of recommendation (occupational)
Support document from the employer for academic leave (where applicable)
Passport bio page, Ghana Card and National Service certificate (where applicable)
selection_criteria: Priority consideration for applicants pursuing Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), special needs programmes, National Initiative Priority programmes, programmes at tuition-free universities, GTEC-nominated lecturers of public tertiary institutions and persons with special needs
Female education - promoting access and equity in education for women and girls - is a named priority area alongside STEM
Vetting and shortlisting of the documents uploaded to the portal, with a rigorous and transparent review and shortlisted candidates contacted afterwards

The scope of the programme expands beyond the traditional 'brilliant but needy' requirement to include capacity building, faculty development, short courses abroad and support for students in international educational competitive programmes
coverage: Sometimes stipend for living expenses - specific details regarding partial or full scholarship are provided upon award
application_method: Create a profile on the GETFund scholarship portal and verify the account
Fill in the online application form and upload all required supporting documents for vetting and shortlisting
Review the application summary and submit
Follow status updates, which are communicated by email and SMS, with further actions continuing through the portal
official.application_route: Online only through the designated GETFund scholarship portal; GETFund states that applications will only be accepted via the designated portal and that all correspondence is conducted exclusively between the Fund and applicants through official channels.
official.international_eligibility: Applicants must be Ghanaian nationals; the 'foreign' element of the scheme is the place of study, not the applicant's nationality, so non-Ghanaians are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Financial support gives high prevalence to Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) programmes and to female education; special dispensation priority also applies to TVET, special needs programmes, National Initiative Priority programmes, programmes at tuition-free universities, lecturers of public tertiary institutions (via GTEC) and persons with special needs
official.research_requirement: A project or research proposal not exceeding five pages is required from Masters and PhD applicants
official.duration: Valid for the postgraduate programme duration as specified in the admission letter, subject to satisfactory academic performance
official.description: The Ghana Education Trust Fund's postgraduate foreign scholarship supports Ghanaian graduates to pursue advanced studies at reputable institutions abroad, providing financial, social and academic support that covers tuition fees, accommodation and scholastic materials. GETFund prioritises STEM programmes and female education, and states that the programme expands beyond the traditional 'brilliant but needy' requirement.
official.program_type: Government trust fund scholarship (postgraduate foreign scholarship)

not_confirmed: the next round's opening and closing dates
verification.notes: No stipend, allowance or scholarship value is published on any GETFund page read; the how-to-apply page states that details of partial or full scholarship are provided upon award, so no amount is asserted and the award is not recorded as fully funded. The 2026/2027 foreign window (13 to 30 April 2026) and the portal-only application route are confirmed on GETFund's own news item.

applicant_utility.summary: This award is aimed at Ghanaian first-degree holders who already have, or can secure, admission to a Master's programme abroad, and the evidence is weighted towards STEM and towards women. The application is entirely portal-based and the documents are vetted before shortlisting, so the practical bottleneck is document quality rather than essays. Note that GETFund leaves the money deliberately vague: coverage is described as tuition, accommodation and scholastic materials, with a stipend only 'sometimes' and the exact partial-or-full position given only on award. Because the 2026/2027 foreign window closed on 30 April 2026, your immediate action is to watch the news page for the 2027/2028 announcement rather than to prepare a late submission.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Ghanaian graduates with at least a second-class first degree and an unconditional or financial-condition offer from an accredited overseas university, ideally in STEM or as a woman, who need tuition and living support to take it up.
application_readiness_checklist: Create and verify your GETFund scholarship portal profile now, so the account is ready when the next foreign round opens
Obtain an admission letter from an accredited university - only unconditional and financial condition letters are accepted, so request this format explicitly from your university
Request the official fee schedule from the university at the same time as the admission letter; both are needed
Draft the project or research proposal to a strict five-page maximum and check that it fits the priority areas
Line up an occupational letter of recommendation and confirm your referees are willing and reachable
Check that your Ghana Card, passport bio page and National Service certificate are current and legible as scans
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an admission letter in the wrong format - only unconditional and financial condition letters are accepted, so provisional or conditional-on-funding letters are rejected
Omitting the fee schedule, which GETFund lists alongside the admission letter as academic documentation
Uploading invisible or unclear scans, which GETFund names explicitly as a disqualifying factor
Exceeding the five-page research proposal limit
Submitting multiple applications, which GETFund describes as instant disqualification
Applying again in the same category if you were already a GETFund Foreign Scholarship beneficiary
Being unable to start by the beginning of the academic year, or already pursuing another Master's or PhD when you apply
Missing the closing date - late and incomplete applications are not considered for assessment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: GETFund states that the foreign scholarship typically covers tuition, accommodation and sometimes a stipend for living expenses, with the exact partial or full position provided only on award. Travel costs, visas and personal expenses are not named anywhere in the published coverage, so plan to fund airfare and visa costs yourself until you have the award terms in writing. Local scholarships under the same programme are explicitly tuition fees only, so do not assume the foreign award behaves identically.
document_audit: Your admission letter must be unconditional or a financial condition letter; anything weaker will not pass vetting
The fee schedule must accompany the admission letter - universities often issue it separately, so chase it early
Certificates and transcripts are required 'where applicable', but omit them only where genuinely not applicable, since missing documentation is a named disqualifier
The research proposal has a hard five-page ceiling, and it is required even at Master's level
The occupational letter of recommendation and the employer's academic leave support letter must come from the right sources; the leave letter is only required where applicable
Every upload must be legible - GETFund specifically disqualifies invisible or unclear documents
alerts: The 2026/2027 foreign round closed on 30 April 2026, so the scheme is not currently accepting applications; the next foreign call is expected in the first half of 2027
Deferment is not permitted - the scholarship must be used for the academic year awarded, so align your offer's start date with the award year
GETFund has separately opened 2026/27 undergraduate and postgraduate LOCAL scholarships, which are tuition-only and are not the same award - do not confuse the two when applying
All correspondence is through official channels only, so treat any approach outside the portal and the Fund's official addresses as suspicious
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create a profile and verify your account on the GETFund portal, complete the form and upload the vetting documents, review the summary and submit, then wait for portal, email and SMS updates through shortlisting; outcomes are only communicated by GETFund through those official channels.
